Room-temperature and high-temperature creep rates
Electrochemical corrosion rates and passivation behavior

hypotheses.label: C11

source_paper.title: Phase-selective recrystallization makes eutectic high-entropy alloys ultra-ductile.

hypotheses.builds_on: The established benefits of surface treatments (such as plasma nitriding) in other high-performance alloys for corrosion and fatigue resistance, combined with the PSR microstructure that provides a strong bulk performance.
hypotheses.what_is_new: This hypothesis proposes a single, post-PSR, surface-tailored intervention (deep plasma nitriding) designed specifically to improve environmental and fatigue-related performance without altering the advantageous bulk microstructure achieved by PSR.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Deep plasma nitriding of the PSR-processed alloy will form a diffusion-based nitride layer that imposes compressive residual stresses and a hardened surface while preserving the bulk duplex microstructure, thereby improving resistance to surface-initiated fatigue, corrosion, and environmental degradation.
hypothesis.material_initial_state: PSR-treated AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a bulk structure comprising a fully recrystallized FCC phase and a recovered skeletal B2 phase.
hypothesis.intervention: Expose the finished alloy to a deep plasma nitriding treatment (e.g., 450–500 °C for 6–8 hours) in a controlled nitrogen atmosphere to allow nitrogen diffusion over a layer of several hundred micrometers.
hypothesis.conditions: The nitriding temperature must be low enough to avoid altering the bulk PSR-modified microstructure. Process parameters should be optimized to ensure uniform nitriding without the formation of brittle nitride networks or excessive case hardness that could lead to spallation.
hypothesis.structural_mediator: The formation of a nitrided surface layer containing fine, dispersed nitride precipitates results in compressive residual stresses and an increased hardness gradient from the surface to the bulk.
hypothesis.mechanism: The nitrided layer acts as a protective barrier against environmental attack and retards surface crack initiation through compressive residual stresses, thereby enhancing fatigue life and resistance to corrosion. This surface strengthening mechanism reduces the likelihood of surface-initiated failure under cyclic thermal and mechanical loads, addressing performance requirements for aerospace fasteners.
hypothesis.predicted_outcome: The plasma-nitrided alloy is expected to show improved resistance to pitting corrosion and delayed fatigue crack initiation compared to the untreated PSR alloy. Improvement in surface-related durability metrics (e.g., a 15–25% increase in the number of cycles to crack initiation) is anticipated, with minimal impact on the bulk ductility.
hypothesis.baseline: The PSR-processed alloy without any post-treatment nitriding.
hypothesis.boundary: Since plasma nitriding primarily modifies the near-surface region, its benefits are confined to surface-initiated failures; if the dominant failure mechanism originates in the bulk, the effect may be limited.
hypothesis.uncertainty: The depth profile of nitrogen diffusion and the exact magnitude of residual compressive stresses must be experimentally optimized, and their translation to improved high-temperature environmental performance remains to be quantified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of PSR alloys: one undergoes deep plasma nitriding under the specified conditions, and one remains untreated. Characterize the nitrided layer using microhardness profiling and XRD residual stress measurements. Then, subject both sets to accelerated corrosion tests (e.g., salt spray, potentiodynamic polarization) and cyclic fatigue testing.
measurements: Microhardness and residual stress profiling (XRD)
Electrochemical corrosion tests
Fatigue testing with surface crack initiation monitoring
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nitrided specimens do not exhibit a significant enhancement in surface hardness, compressive residual stress magnitude, and delayed crack initiation or improved corrosion resistance relative to the control specimens, the hypothesis is falsified.

hypotheses.label: C5

hypothesis.hypothesis: Minor Mo addition will stabilize the Al-Ni-rich B2 phase by promoting a more protective Mo-containing passive film, thereby reducing selective dissolution and pitting corrosion while maintaining a good strength–ductility balance.
hypothesis.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy exhibiting a dual-phase lamellar structure with Al–Ni-rich B2 regions that show high dislocation density and are prone to selective dissolution under chloride-containing acid conditions.
hypothesis.intervention: Introduce a minor addition (≈1–2 atomic %) of molybdenum (Mo) during alloy melting.
hypothesis.conditions: Maintain the overall eutectic composition and casting process so that the refined microstructure (lamellar spacing) is preserved. Experiments would be performed in chloride-containing sulfuric acid solutions at temperatures ranging from 5 °C to 60 °C.
hypothesis.structural_mediator: Preferential partitioning of Mo into the B2 phase, where it forms Mo-oxides that enhance passive film stability and reduce the galvanic coupling with the L12 phase.
hypothesis.mechanism: Mo is known to improve the corrosion resistance in stainless steels by stabilizing passive films. In the current HEA, Mo is expected to replace or modify part of the Al–Ni-rich phase characteristics, reducing the formation rate of defects (like oxygen vacancies) in the passive film and slowing down the pitting corrosion mechanism observed at elevated temperatures.
hypothesis.predicted_outcome: Reduced passive current densities, higher pitting potentials, and decreased selective dissolution of the B2 phase. Overall, an improvement in corrosion resistance by an expected moderate margin relative to the baseline, while maintaining or slightly enhancing the mechanical balance.
hypothesis.baseline: Performance of the unmodified AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy showing increased passive current and selective corrosion of the B2 phase in chloride-containing solutions, especially at elevated temperatures.
hypothesis.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected provided the Mo content is kept low enough to avoid formation of excessive intermetallic phases or disrupting the eutectic structure. The improvement is valid only in environments similar to the tested acid solution and temperature range.
hypothesis.uncertainty: Moderate; the precise segregation behavior of Mo and its effect on the passive film in this multi-principal element system may vary, and optimization of the Mo content is critical.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloys—one standard AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and one modified with 1–2 at.% Mo—with identical processing conditions. Expose samples to 0.005 M H2SO4 + 0.05 M NaCl solutions at various temperatures (e.g., 25 °C and 60 °C) and perform potentiodynamic polarization and EIS tests.
measurements: Passive current density
Pitting potential
EIS-derived charge transfer resistance
Microstructural analysis and phase partitioning (via EBSD/EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Mo-modified alloy does not show significantly lower passive current densities or increased pitting potentials (beyond experimental error) compared to the control, or if detrimental phases form that compromise the microstructure, the hypothesis is falsified.

hypotheses.label: C12

hypothesis.conditions: Directional solidification must be controlled to yield a high thermal gradient and reproducible, oriented lamellar spacing; subsequent thermo-mechanical processing (rolling/annealing) should be adjusted to maintain the alignment.
hypothesis.structural_mediator: Aligned, continuous lamellar interfaces with refined and uniformly distributed phase spacing.

hypothesis.uncertainty: Exact magnitude improvements in strength–ductility and creep resistance remain to be quantified.

Room-temperature creep rate and high-temperature steady state creep rate
Electrochemical corrosion potential and pit density
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the directionally solidified samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in yield strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance compared to the conventional samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

hypotheses.label: C3

hypotheses.what_is_new: This hypothesis introduces an innovative casting intervention—electromagnetic stirring—to refine the eutectic microstructure, an approach not employed in the paper, aimed at simultaneously improving strength, ductility, and long-term performance under mechanical and corrosive conditions.

hypothesis.material_initial_state: Standard as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA produced by conventional casting, featuring a lamellar fcc/B2 structure with ~2 μm interlamellar spacing.

hypothesis.conditions: Casting under similar overall conditions, with the addition of an electromagnetic stirring system applied during solidification. hypothesis.structural_mediator: A refined, uniformly distributed eutectic lamellar structure with decreased interlamellar spacing and reduced compositional segregation.

A more homogeneous microstructure can also reduce the likelihood of localized corrosion initiation and improve creep resistance by limiting diffusion pathways. Fundamentally, controlled stirring reduces macro- and micro-segregation, ensuring that the eutectic phases form more uniformly, which is beneficial for long-term mechanical stability.
hypothesis.predicted_outcome: An improvement in yield and fracture strength due to refined microstructural features, possibly with a modest increase in ductility (owing to more homogeneous plastic deformation) and enhanced creep and corrosion resistance. hypothesis.baseline: The conventional, as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy with a 2 μm lamellar spacing and some degree of compositional segregation.
hypothesis.boundary: This intervention is particularly relevant for casting processes; its benefits may be limited if the stirring parameters are not carefully optimized. Excessively high stirring could lead to turbulence-induced defects.
hypothesis.uncertainty: The precise quantitative gain in strength and durability is uncertain and must be optimized against potential defects; the benefits on creep and corrosion are inferred but need experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Cast batches of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with and without electromagnetic stirring under otherwise identical conditions. Tensile and yield strength measurements
Creep deformation under constant load
Corrosion resistance metrics (e.g., pit density, corrosion rate)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If samples produced with electromagnetic stirring do not exhibit a significantly refined microstructure and corresponding improvements in mechanical, creep, or corrosion performance compared to unstirred samples, the hypothesis would be falsified.

hypotheses.label: C6

hypothesis.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a lamellar microstructure in which the B2 phase exhibits a relatively high dislocation density and serves as a site for preferential corrosion initiation.

hypothesis.predicted_outcome: A reduction in the passive current densities and a delayed onset of pitting corrosion, along with modest improvements in low-temperature creep resistance due to lower defect concentrations. hypothesis.baseline: The original AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy with high dislocation density in the B2 phase that exhibits accelerated corrosion and passive film degradation in chloride-containing acid solutions.
hypothesis.boundary: The effectiveness of the annealing treatment is limited by the need to avoid excessive coarsening of the microstructure; the treatment window must be carefully controlled so that recovery is achieved without causing detrimental phase growth or loss of the fine eutectic structure.
hypothesis.uncertainty: Moderate to high; while reducing dislocations is known to improve corrosion resistance in many alloys, the optimal annealing parameters for this HEA system are not yet established and risk altering the delicate balance between phases.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy specimens: one set in the as-cast condition and one set subjected to the specified annealing treatment. Passive current and pitting potentials from electrochemical tests
Microstructural characterization to ensure lamellar integrity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in dislocation density or improved corrosion performance (e.g., similar passive current density and pitting behavior) compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

Stress–strain curves and work hardening rates
Creep strain rates under fixed high-temperature loading
Corrosion pit density under accelerated corrosion testing

Corrosion rates and pit density
